title: 1976-09-15_Dorothy_160.txt
concise_summary: In this dense Exegesis entry PKD argues that his novel Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said functions as an involuntary steganographic vehicle: God (working through the Holy Spirit as 'Thomas') penetrated the novel and embedded an apocalyptic message that we are living in the Roman Empire circa A.D. 70 and that Christ's return is imminent. PKD develops a theory of divine syzygy — the soul's ontological fusion with Christ through the abolition of linear time and Christian anamnesis — as the mechanism by which the 2-3-74 experience transformed him. In the entry's second movement, he critiques F.M. Cornford's reading of Ananke and Will Durant's instrumentalist philosophy-of-religion, arguing that the true purpose of religion is not to explain suffering but to enlist a God powerful enough to break the imprisoning astral template of fate and actively redirect a person's life.
key_claims: Flow My Tears was not written by PKD in the ordinary sense; the divine entity (working through 'Thomas') penetrated the novel and used it as a steganographic vehicle to encode the message that we are prisoners living in Rome c. A.D. 70 and that the savior is about to return.
The Xerox Missive was a forgery sent by an underground network that knew the suppressed truth encoded in Flow My Tears, intended to silence PKD before he could decode or broadcast that truth.

PKD was operating as unwitting 'bait': his 2-3-74 experience and his handling of the Xerox Missive together served a divine tactical purpose, luring an evil agent into the open so that Thomas could destroy it.

The mechanism of salvation is ontological syzygy — the person's identity is exchanged with Christ's through the abolition of linear time; through Christian anamnesis one does not merely resemble Christ but ontologically becomes him.

The purpose of Christianity and mystery religion is not to explain undeserved suffering (contra Durant) but to invoke a God powerful enough to intervene and break the deterministic astral template (Ananke) that imprisons a person.

F.M. Cornford errs in reading Ananke as mere errant chance; the ancient Near Eastern (Babylonian) astrological tradition shows that a fixed deterministic outcome — fate — was fully grasped, and the god who can shatter that template is analogous to Plato's Nous.
recurring_concepts: Steganography / latent message: hidden apocalyptic truth encoded in popular fiction and rock music
Thomas: the discarnate Roman-era alter-ego who possesses PKD and acts through him
Syzygy: the ontological pairing of a human soul with Christ, replicating the original Jesus/Christ union
Christian anamnesis: the abolition of linear time allowing one to participate in the eternally-enacted ur-drama of Christ's passion and resurrection
Ananke: the imprisoning astral-fate template PKD derives from Greek and Babylonian cosmology
The Artifact: the spurious, evil world-system constructed by a blind or malign power, unable to detect God's invisible penetration and replacement of its victims
The Ur-drama / Eidos: the Platonic archetype of suffering-death-rebirth of which individual ordeals are copies
Disinhibition stimulus: embedded trigger elements in the novel (the dream sequence, the command 'Felix', the gas-station scene) that unlock suppressed awareness of the true situation
people_entities: Thomas: PKD's name for the first-century Christian alter-ego personality that emerged in 2-3-74 and acts through him
Pinky: unidentified person (possibly a neighbor or acquaintance) in whom PKD claims to have externally observed the Christ-transformation
Father Rasch: a priest or clergyman who helped PKD link what he saw in 2-3-74 with the material in Flow My Tears
F.M. Cornford: British classicist (1874-1943), author of work on Greek cosmology; PKD disputes his reading of Ananke
Will Durant: American historian and philosopher (1885-1981); PKD disputes Durant's claim that religion's purpose is to explain undeserved suffering
Martin Luther: German theologian (1483-1546); quoted approvingly for the phrase 'the very desperate' as those who fall within Christ's province
Plato: Greek philosopher; his concept of Nous is cited as an analogue for the God who breaks Ananke
Hegel: German philosopher; cited for his notion of God acting upon human history as material
Satan: the adversarial power over whom God (as voluntary sacrifice) holds ultimate power
Jesus Christ: the discorporate Lord whose Holy Spirit is the agent of identity exchange and syzygy
texts_works: Acts of the Apostles (New Testament): PKD identifies material from Acts as embedded in Flow My Tears and sees Acts as describing the early apostolic church of Rome c. A.D. 70
The Bible: referenced generally as the scriptural frame for PKD's Rome-A.D.-70 chronotope
F.M. Cornford (unnamed title): PKD critiques Cornford's philosophical interpretation of Ananke
Will Durant (unnamed title, possibly The Story of Philosophy or The Story of Civilization): PKD disputes Durant's philosophy-of-religion thesis
autobiographical: PKD describes his receipt of and response to the 'Xerox Missive' — a threatening or misleading document he believes was a forgery sent by a network suppressing the truth embedded in Flow My Tears
PKD states that in the same month Flow My Tears was released, he was independently 'shown the truth' about the Rome A.D. 70 chronotope, and that Father Rasch helped him link the vision to the novel

PKD identifies his 2-3-74 (February-March 1974) experience as an instance of the divine syzygy: the 'old man' was broken and he experienced the new life — resurrection — in this world rather than death
PKD claims he observed the Christ-transformation externally in a person named Pinky, while he experienced it internally without knowing what it was at the time
PKD describes being 'bait' for an evil power during the Xerox Missive episode, and credits Thomas with using him to neutralize 'a crucial link in some evil chain of action'
theological_motifs: Theosis / deification: 'God became man so that man could become God' — the patristic formula applied to PKD's 2-3-74 experience
Voluntary divine sacrifice: God as surrogate victim who has no power held over him by Satan
The Passion and victorious resurrection: Christ's suffering leads not to extinction but to joy and eternal life; he returns not to die again but as triumphant judge and king
The 'old man' and the 'new man': the Pauline stripping-away of the worldly self as prerequisite for divine transformation
Theodicy by over-offsetting: justice is not established but injustice is overwhelmed by an excess of divine counter-action
Mystery religion as divine contact: PKD distinguishes the purpose of mystery religions (putting humans in touch with an intervening God) from philosophy (reconciling humans to fate)
Apocalyptic imminence: the savior has already deeply penetrated the world in his first role as surrogate victim and will imminently return as judge and king
Sacred vs. mundane time: the distinction between linear historical time and the sacred time in which the original Passion is perpetually enacted
DNA engramming as ancestral determinism: PKD speculates whether the Thomas personality represents a summa form of ancestral (DNA-encoded) fate
literary_self_ref: Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said: PKD argues the novel contains material unmistakably drawn from Acts of the Apostles and encodes the steganographic message that we live in Rome c. A.D. 70, with a dream sequence, the name 'Felix', and a gas-station scene with a Black man functioning as disinhibition triggers

The Unteleported Man: PKD draws a structural parallel — just as the coded message in that novel gets back to Earth revealing what the colony is really like, so Flow My Tears encodes the true nature of present reality
symbols_images: The Xerox Missive: a physical forged document received by PKD, operating as the adversary's attempt to silence him and as the trap that PKD-as-bait set for the evil power
The all-night gas station and the Black man: a scene from Flow My Tears that PKD identifies as a disinhibition trigger embedded in the novel
The 'thief in the night': biblical image of the unexpected manifestation of the savior, quoted approvingly
Birthpangs: PKD figures the pains of the divine ordeal as literally the pains of spiritual birth
The imprisoning astral template: a deterministic overlay on a person's life, derived from Babylonian astrological fate, that God alone can shatter
The Trojan prince bound to seek Italian land: a classical example (Aeneas/Aeneid) PKD uses to illustrate Ananke as fixed destination even if the process is not deterministic
tensions: PKD oscillates between claiming he consciously 'smoked out' the evil network and insisting he was unwitting bait who did not know his true role — agency and passivity are simultaneously asserted
PKD says he always believed the cypher US intelligence suspected in Flow My Tears was not there, but immediately entertains the possibility that it was — undermining his own prior certainty

The entry states PKD 'didn't know it, and didn't write it' regarding the steganographic content of Flow My Tears, yet earlier entries (and this one) show him actively decoding the novel as if he had intended the meanings — the line between authorial unconscious and divine dictation is unstable

PKD speculates that Thomas might be a 'summa form of ancestral determinism' (DNA engramming) but also insists Thomas is the liberating agent who breaks determinism — the Thomas-personality is simultaneously the instrument of fate and its destroyer

PKD cannot fully explain why, unlike others who undergo the ordeal, he experienced resurrection 'here' rather than death — he says they were able to 'break the matrix' for him, but offers no mechanism, leaving this as a privileged but unexplained exception
evidence_quotes: "I saw what evil (blind + deterministic) cannot see: speculation: I was bait, + not what the evil power thought, nor what even I thought."

"God became man so that man could become God - This is accomplished (the latter) by an exchange of identities: (man) that a two-way thrust of personality. Suddenly the time + place is Rome c AD70. suddenly the person, the man, is not himself; he - the 'I' in him - is another 'I.'"

"This syzygy with the divine (a replication of The Jesus/Christ original syzygy of man + the divine) is (as I know through experience of it) accomplished through the abolition of process (linear) time + space, + a penetrating to the eternally-enacted ur-drama. This is Xtian anamnesis, a remembering of identity. Through this we are him, not like but are."
"Theodicy is achieved not by establishing justice but by over-offsetting injustice."
"it is the purpose of philosophy to explain + reconcile man to his fate; but God has the power to change (deflect) that fate. God is a higher power, not just a wiser one."
uncertainty_flags: Pinky: the identity of this person is entirely unclear; it is unknown whether Pinky is a neighbor, a friend, or a fictional name, and what transformation PKD claims to have witnessed
Father Rasch: no further identification is given; it is unclear whether this is a Catholic priest PKD knew personally or a more incidental encounter, and what specific interpretive help he provided

The Xerox Missive: PKD is certain it was a forgery but provides no corroborating evidence; the 'network' he claims to have smoked out is entirely conjectural and the threat may be paranoid elaboration

The claim that Flow My Tears was 'penetrated by the divine': PKD asserts this but simultaneously says he did not write the hidden content and did not know it was there — the epistemological basis for his certainty is unclear

The Cornford reference: PKD does not name the specific work; the classicist F.M. Cornford wrote on Plato's cosmology (Plato's Cosmology) and Greek philosophy of nature, but which text PKD is engaging is unspecified

PKD's claim that 'the message in Tears is only one part of a total message woven into many books and rock music' implies a vast hidden conspiracy of steganographic truth-telling, but no other works or artists are identified
